reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses Ni-containing coatings on diamond particles for HEA matrices, showing improved wettability and metallurgical bonding via carbide-forming elements, but it does not address W–Cu systems, transient liquid formation, or fusion-reactor conditions. The key premises about Ni–Cu transient liquid behavior, void filling, and property enhancement in W–Cu are unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Ni coating on W particles can be applied uniformly by chemical solution deposition below 400°C
During SPS at ~1200°C, the Ni coating will partially react with Cu to form a transient liquid phase
This transient Ni–Cu liquid will spread along W surfaces, fill microvoids, and reduce interfacial energy
The resulting graded interface will reduce phase separation and improve thermal/mechanical properties vs. uncoated SPS
The approach avoids excessive brittle intermetallics if coating thickness and sintering are optimized
